clue.text: Swap hobby, perhaps, for business's seasonal ups and downs

parts.note: to swap goods is to trade them
a hobby-horse was an early pedal-less bicycle, so a hobby is one kind of cycle

explanation.surface: Someone exchanges a pastime for a study of how business rises and falls through the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The hobby-horse, or dandy horse, was a nineteenth-century forerunner of the bicycle; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use this term for the recurring expansion and contraction of commercial activity.

clue.text: Restrain employee taking smack

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand or factory hand
a cuff is a light blow with the open hand

explanation.surface: A boss holds back a worker who has been hitting people.
explanation.definitionFit: To put metal rings on someone's wrists is to restrain them, so the verb fits.

clue.text: One Eddy agitated

parts.note: one is A, as in 'a pound' for one pound
an eddy of water or air is a swirl

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy is in a nervous state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name, but it is the whirlpool, which gives SWIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in a whirling, churned-up state is stirred up or disturbed, the adjective sense here.

clue.text: Resident of Paradise Avenue's westernmost block

indicators.note: in an across-reading word the western end is the left, so this picks the first letter of the word Avenue

parts.note: a dam blocks a river

explanation.surface: A property advert describes the far west building on Paradise Avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paradise Avenue' reads as a street name, but Paradise belongs with the definition: Eden's first man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man lived in the Garden of Eden, which is Paradise.

clue.text: Mountaineer wouldn't want to have this Arabic hoop rotating

definitions.text: Mountaineer wouldn't want to have this

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber would not like to be spun about inside an Arabic hoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' rearranges ARABIC and HOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear of heights is the last thing someone scaling peaks would wish for.

clue.text: Do battle as a clear starter?

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
the Somme was a major First World War battle in 1916

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether fighting counts as a plain first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of the Somme was fought in northern France in 1916; the question mark flags that a clear soup is one kind of starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear meat broth served as the first course of a meal is the dish meant.

clue.text: Noble needs to move slowly out of heroin chic

indicators.note: means the letters for 'move slowly' are taken away from the phrase heroin chic

parts.note: to inch is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: A fashion commentator says a gallant figure must edge away from the gaunt heroin-chic look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heroin chic' was a 1990s fashion look of pale, gaunt models; remove INCH from HEROINCHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and high-minded behaviour is noble in spirit, the adjective meant here.

clue.text: Upped paper round's load

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue upped means the word is read from bottom to top, turning it round

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A newsagent complains that the paper round has become heavier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; in a down clue 'Upped' means read from the bottom, and 'paper round' looks like a newspaper delivery job.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or responsibility one has to carry is a load in the figurative sense.

clue.text: "Bride's Vow Rejected" in C sharp — terribly moving, musically

indicators.note: one group of letters is placed inside the other
C and sharp are taken badly out of order and rearranged
the vow is turned back to front, as something thrown back

parts.note: the bride says 'I do' at the wedding

explanation.surface: A song titled Bride's Vow Rejected, written in C sharp, is described as very moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges C and sharp; 'Rejected' turns the bride's vow back to front, and 'in' places it inside before the final C. The quoted title disguises the pieces as a song name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is an emotional free-form piece, so the adjective means emotionally stirring in a musical way.

clue.text: Lines about cinema

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, a set of lines
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Some verses written about the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a well-known British cinema chain, and the name became a byword for a picture house.

clue.text: Art movement's block flooring that's raised inside

indicators.note: the raised floor goes within the word for block

parts.note: a dam blocks a river
a dais is a raised platform of floor

explanation.surface: An art movement's block of flooring has a raised section inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' looks like part of the art, but it is DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century anti-art movement, and this is the name for its doctrine.

clue.text: Bony so-and-so, contorted with use

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: read literally, so and so gives the word so twice

explanation.surface: Someone calls a skinny person a so-and-so, twisted by use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-and-so' looks like an insult, but it is SO + SO; 'contorted' rearranges SOSO with USE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the scientific adjective for things made of or like bone.

clue.text: Hard workhouse fare, cold, not good

indicators.note: means good is dropped and cold put in its place

parts.note: gruel, thin porridge, was the diet in Victorian workhouses, as in Oliver Twist
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Workhouse food was harsh: cold and bad.
explanation.walkthrough: In GRUEL, swap G (good) for C (cold), as 'cold, not good' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, in the sense of harsh or unkind to others, is a synonym.

clue.text: Armed forces cut back: march organised, ending in Aldershot

indicators.note: means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to hew is to cut with blows

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order
takes the final letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: Troops are cut back while a march is arranged, finishing in Aldershot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns HEW into WEH; 'organised' rearranges MARCH into RMACH. Aldershot is a British army garrison town in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wehrmacht was the combined military of Nazi Germany, its army, navy and air force.

clue.text: Won six — best flipping place for making a telling court appearance

definitions.text: place for making a telling court appearance

indicators.note: the letters are flipped about into another order

explanation.surface: A cricket team won by six wickets and best; the court reference follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it rearranges WON SIX BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the enclosure where a witness stands to give evidence in a court.

clue.text: Become fond of work and dress down

parts.note: to take to someone is to start liking them
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Grow to like your job and then dress casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress down' looks like casual clothing, but here it means to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is to reprimand them severely, an idiom for scolding.

clue.text: It's not really intended to be read on the surface in a lounge environment

definitions.text: It's not really intended to be read on the surface in a lounge environment

parts.words: It's not really intended to be read on the surface in a lounge environment
parts.note: a large glossy illustrated volume left lying on a low living-room table, meant for show rather than reading

explanation.definitionFit: Such big picture volumes are displayed on low sitting-room tables to be browsed more than read.

clue.text: National English top grade in typing wangled

indicators.note: the top grade goes inside the rearranged letters
fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the top mark in exams

explanation.surface: A English student got the top mark for typing by fiddling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wangled' rearranges TYPING into GYPTIN, with A put 'in' before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; this one is a citizen of Egypt.

clue.text: Into the race, nobbled horse is a little bit at sea

parts.note: 'they're off' means the runners are under way, so off means into the race

indicators.note: a nobbled horse has been tampered with, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A tampered-with horse joins the race and is a bit lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nobbled' (British slang for drugging a racehorse) rearranges HORSE into SHORE. 'at sea' suggests confusion, but means out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something positioned a short way out from the coast on the water is located there.

clue.text: Sheep may start to mate playfully: it will progress into a far from jolly wheeze

definitions.text: it will progress into a far from jolly wheeze

indicators.note: the letters frolic about into a new order
takes the first letter of the word mate

explanation.surface: Sheep may begin to mate in play, though the wheeze that follows is no joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playfully' rearranges SHEEP, MAY and M (the start of mate). 'wheeze' looks like a joke or scheme, but it is laboured breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: This lung disease worsens over time and leaves sufferers breathless and wheezing.

clue.text: Indian dish is reverse of a soft, mushy okra

indicators.note: the a and the soft letter are read in the opposite order

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft

indicators.note: soft and pulped, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An Indian dish is the opposite of soft, mushy okra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns A + P into PA; 'mushy' rearranges OKRA into KORA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pakora is a battered and deep-fried vegetable fritter from Indian cooking.

clue.text: Possess the right qualities for live attack

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: Someone has what it takes to face a living attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit or be appropriate for something means having qualities right for it.

clue.text: Foils one stored in holds

indicators.note: the letter is kept within the word for holds

parts.note: a ship's bulk is its cargo hold
one is A

explanation.surface: Fencing swords, one of them, are kept in a ship's holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foils' looks like fencing swords; it is a verb meaning thwarts.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart or frustrate someone is to block them, the verb meant.

clue.text: Skis three times around the island

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time, so three times gives three Ts

explanation.surface: Someone skis three laps round the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container word, but here it is the anagram signal for the skis and the three Ts together.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean island is part of the federation with Nevis.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink account

definitions.meaning: a Japanese rice wine served warm or cold
as in 'on my account', meaning for my benefit or interest

explanation.surface: A bill for drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese rice wine is one sense; the other is a person's benefit or interest, as in 'for your own good'.

clue.text: Having rowdy sex is to live, basically

parts.note: rough means boisterous or rowdy
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Wild sex is said to be the essence of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basically' looks like 'essentially', but it means in a basic way, without comforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Camping without comforts is to live in primitive conditions, as the idiom means.

clue.text: It's not cheap, making legal documents sound

indicators.note: means the word for legal documents is heard rather than seen

parts.note: writs are formal court orders

explanation.surface: Legal paperwork is expensive, as it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ritz is a luxury hotel in London, and 'ritzy' means expensively smart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz hotel is famously expensive, so it is described as not cheap.

clue.text: What is in store for some? Ford model (without wing)

definitions.text: What is in store for some?

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so the car's name wraps round the wing

parts.note: the Ka is a small Ford car
an arm of a building or organisation is a wing

explanation.surface: Some wonder what is coming; a Ford car is missing a wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it is the old sense outside, so the small car wraps around the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief, the fate awaiting someone depends on deeds; 'some' marks that not everyone believes this.

clue.text: Fringes unfashionable on garments

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
skirts are garments

explanation.surface: Fringes on clothes are no longer in style.
explanation.definitionFit: The edges of a town or area are its fringes, a plural noun synonym.
